newsitem.title: USA: GM applauds new air bag rules.
newsitem.headline: GM applauds new air bag rules.

text.p: General Motors Corp said it welcomed federal air bag actions announced Friday, which will allow GM to install de-powered air bags in vehicles two years earlier than would have been possible under the previous rules.

The world's largest automaker said it plans to begin introducing cars with de-powered air bags this summer. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said Friday it will permit automakers to reduce the deployment power of air bags by as much as 35 percent to save lives.
GM said the new rules will allow the industry to utilize a new sled test protocol that moves up by two years installation of de-powered air bags.
"We applaud Dr. Ricardo Martinez and the NHTSA for their quick response in approving the new testing protocol," said Robert Lange, GM's director of safety engineering, in a statement.
"We anticipate that de-powering air bags in GM vehicles will virtually eliminate inflation risk to adults and will substantially reduce the risk to small children," he said.
